match.reason: The bank point is about a business owner weighing a business against other options, which is narrower than the new point's general lesson that higher-return investments like shares carry more risk than safer ones like term deposits, and it comes from a different subject and depth.

draft.title: Risk and return
card: Return is what an investment earns, such as interest, payments or a rise in value. Risk is the chance you earn less than you hoped, or lose some of your money.
Investments that can earn more usually carry more risk. Shares can rise a lot in value, but their price can also fall, so you might get back less than you put in.
A term deposit is safer. The interest rate is agreed in advance and the bank returns your money, but the return is usually lower.
Investors weigh how much risk they can accept against the return they want. Spreading money across different investments can reduce the harm if one does badly.
draft.remember: Higher possible return usually comes with higher risk of loss.

a.q: Compared with a term deposit, what do shares usually offer?
opts: A chance of higher returns with more risk of loss
A lower return with less risk of loss
A guaranteed return set in advance
A higher return with no risk of loss
a.why: Shares can earn more but their prices can fall, so they carry more risk. A term deposit is the one with an agreed rate, which is why a guaranteed return is wrong for shares.
a.clue: Which one has a price that moves up and down?

b.q: Priya needs her savings back in one year for a car and cannot afford to lose any. Which choice suits her best?
opts: A term deposit, because the return is agreed and safer
Shares, because they usually earn more over time
Shares, because their prices only rise in a year
A term deposit, because it always earns the most
b.why: Priya cannot afford a loss, so she should take the safer option with an agreed return. Shares may earn more, but their price can fall, and a term deposit usually earns less, not the most.
b.clue: She cannot accept a loss, so which one is safer?

a.best: A chance of higher returns with more risk of loss

b.best: A term deposit, because the return is agreed and safer

problems.detail: The right option stands out: it is the longest and the only one with a qualifier ('A chance of'), so a student could pick it without knowing the idea.
Two wrong options use absolute words ('always earns the most', 'only rise'), which mark them as wrong and leave the right option easy to pick by elimination.

check.summary: The facts are correct and both questions have one clear right answer. In question a the right option is the longest and the only hedged one, and in question b the absolute words 'always' and 'only' give away the wrong options.
